page: Microsoft Azure D2plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance belonging to the DPLDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor based on the ARMv8 architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz, the CPU provides 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core.

For storage, the instance includes a 77 GB local disk and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. It does not feature any bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Hardware-level cryptographic acceleration is supported via the AES instruction set, though other advanced vector and matrix extensions such as AVX or AMX are absent.

Benchmark evaluations indicate modest performance characteristics. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression both register in the average range. However, multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and memory bandwidth tests fall into the weak to poor categories, with uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measured at 26.37 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also positioned in the lower tiers, reflecting the resource-constrained nature of this low-memory profile.

This server type represents a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring dedicated ARM physical cores without high memory demands. It is best suited for lightweight applications, basic web serving, software compilation tasks, and development or testing environments that do not require extensive memory capacity or high-throughput parallel processing.

This low-memory, cost-efficient configuration is designed for lightweight workloads, including basic web serving, software compilation, and development environments that benefit from dedicated ARM architecture without requiring high memory density.
